bug_semantics: An authenticated backend user who can reach a list view supplied by a plugin with a Backend\Widgets\Filter numberrange scope and a conditions string can send attacker-controlled JSON numbers to onFilterUpdate(). numbersFromAjax() used /\d/ as its entire validation rule, so any string containing one digit (for example, a numeric prefix followed by SQL syntax) survived unchanged. applyScopeToQuery() then used strtr() to splice the two values into the configured conditions and passed the resulting SQL to whereRaw(), making the suffix executable SQL. The prerequisite combination is not used by built-in Winter CMS views, so a vanilla installation without such a plugin is not exploitable.
flaw_origin: The numberrange scaffolding and unsafe strtr()/whereRaw() sink first appeared in be87fbbb8751d6c6b81e473f381fb4c62b5e7ffe, but that commit called a nonexistent numbersFromAjax() method and omitted the numberrange template, so the shipped path was not functional. Its immediate child a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 is the smallest true BIC: it added the missing template and implemented numbersFromAjax() with the permissive /\d/ predicate while retaining the raw interpolation sink, thereby completing the exploitable source-to-sink path. This is a direct one-parent commit, not a move, revert, backport, release commit, or squash aggregate.
ai_marker: No AI marker in the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60` shows author and committer Luke Towers <luke@luketowers.ca>, one parent, the subject `Cleanup for #2856`, and a human-written explanatory body; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/wintercms/winter/security/advisories/GHSA-m7jc-g4rc-jmvh identifies the numberrange-plus-conditions attack prerequisites, authenticated backend access, affected winter/wn-backend-module versions <= 1.2.12, patched version 1.2.13, and direct fix 50713de95adf5298536d93f4d999652525d36d43.

Run `git show --format=fuller --no-renames be87fbbb8751d6c6b81e473f381fb4c62b5e7ffe -- modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php`: it introduces the numberrange AJAX branch and the conditions sink `whereRaw(DbDongle::parse(strtr(... ':min' => $min, ':max' => $max)))`, but invokes numbersFromAjax() without defining it. `git cat-file -e be87fbbb8751d6c6b81e473f381fb4c62b5e7ffe:modules/backend/widgets/filter/partials/_scope_numberrange.htm` also fails because the template is absent.

Run `git show --format=fuller --no-renames a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 -- modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php modules/backend/widgets/filter/partials/_scope_numberrange.htm`: this child adds the missing template and the missing numbersFromAjax() implementation, whose `$numberRegex = '/\d/';` and preg_match checks preserve an entire attacker string whenever it contains any digit. `git rev-parse a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60^` returns be87fbbb8751d6c6b81e473f381fb4c62b5e7ffe.

Direct parent absence is reproducible with `git grep -n -F 'protected function numbersFromAjax' be87fbbb8751d6c6b81e473f381fb4c62b5e7ffe -- modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php` (no match) versus the same command at a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 (line 909). Thus the parent contains incomplete scaffolding and the raw sink but lacks the validator/source method and render template required for the real vulnerable path.

History cross-check: `git log --all --reverse --format='%H %ad %s' -S"$numberRegex = '/\\d/';" -- modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php` starts at a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60. `git log -L '/protected function numbersFromAjax/,/^    }/':modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php 50713de95adf5298536d93f4d999652525d36d43^` likewise shows a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 adding the function, followed only by 9b72c2d181ce3c121abf54949809e760113d2f5b changing invalid-array handling while retaining the permissive predicate.

The pre-fix source-to-sink path is visible at fix parent 555e67c84b503b60aa0a5775382087c5da97b7ca: modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php lines 302-315 decode posted options, call numbersFromAjax(), and store the range; lines 845-858 splice min/max into conditions passed to whereRaw(); lines 1094-1114 accept any value matching /\d/.

Run `git show --format=fuller --no-renames 50713de95adf5298536d93f4d999652525d36d43 -- modules/backend/widgets/Filter.php`: the direct fix replaces /\d/ with is_numeric(), casts accepted values to float, replaces inline strtr() substitution with positional placeholders and bindings through processConditionBindings(), and supplies those bindings to whereRaw(). Its sole parent is 555e67c84b503b60aa0a5775382087c5da97b7ca, where the vulnerable code remains.

Release ancestry confirms both ends. `git tag --contains a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 --sort=version:refname` begins at v1.0.421; `git merge-base --is-ancestor a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 v1.0.420` is false and the same check against v1.0.421 and v1.2.12 is true. `git tag --contains 50713de95adf5298536d93f4d999652525d36d43 --sort=version:refname` begins at v1.2.13; the fix is not an ancestor of v1.2.12 but is an ancestor of v1.2.13. v1.2.12 resolves to b6ac66c5e80ddc9ecd9211c10204cdcee6e14313 and v1.2.13 to e09c8d3526f3583cb6c3476a021b885088ecd4bd.

reasoning: The advisory mechanism is borne out by the pre-fix code: untrusted posted range strings pass a contains-a-digit check unchanged and are then interpolated into raw SQL. Although be87fbbb8751d6c6b81e473f381fb4c62b5e7ffe wrote the unsafe sink, it left the feature unusable because its called parser and template did not exist. The immediately following a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 completed that exact path with the flawed validator, and its parent directly lacks the completed vulnerability, so a705a70f3560d645d4864996282ec0923fcb9e60 is the smallest causal BIC. The advisory-linked commit directly closes both input acceptance and SQL construction, and tag ancestry matches the <=1.2.12 / 1.2.13 boundary. Finally, the BIC commit object contains only a named human author/committer and no AI-generating or co-author marker, so under the BIC-only rule the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
